clue.text: Fluid rise complete, predator rampant?

indicators.note: a rampant beast rears up on its hind legs, so in a down entry the word climbs and reads bottom to top

explanation.surface: A rearing predator seems to be part of some description of rising liquid.
explanation.walkthrough: The wolf is reversed so it reads upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: An upflow is a current of liquid or gas moving upwards, so a rising stream.

clue.text: Washing going on the line, all there

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a load of laundry pegged out side by side on a clothes line
second meaning: coherent, making sense as a whole

explanation.surface: Laundry pegged out on the line, every item present and correct.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is literal: clothes hung up side by side; the second is the idiom for an argument or a mind that is coherent.
explanation.definitionFit: 'All there' means of sound mind, and hanging together means being consistent and coherent.

clue.text: See 13
Dubious item with talented nun, art — is it?

definitions.text: Dubious item with talented nun, art — is it?

indicators.note: something dubious is questionable and not straight, so the following letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A questionable piece involving a gifted nun is art, is it? Someone sounds sceptical.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a racy show featuring a 'talented nun' is the kind of thing whose claim to be art one doubts.
explanation.definitionFit: Adult entertainment is the euphemism for sexually explicit shows, whose artistic merit is famously doubtful.

clue.text: Italian author pilloried, lingua vulgaris!

indicators.note: mock Latin for common or coarse, the debased version of the language, so the words before it are mangled

explanation.surface: An Italian writer attacked in coarse, common language.
explanation.definitionFit: Luigi Pirandello was the Nobel-winning Italian playwright of Six Characters in Search of an Author.

clue.text: Saucy American oath arising in vacuous country

indicators.note: the American and the oath sit inside the emptied word
vacuous means empty, so the word loses all its inside letters and only its ends are kept

parts.note: US is the standard abbreviation for American

indicators.note: in a down entry rising means reading from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A cheeky American swearword going up in some empty land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saucy' looks like cheeky; read literally it means like a sauce, and custard is a sweet sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Custardy describes something like custard, the pouring sauce served with puddings.

clue.text: What nutmeg grater has done for breakfast item

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the phrase nutmeg grater has taken in a three-letter breakfast item across its two words
second meaning: a dish cooked by simmering out of its shell

explanation.surface: Some kitchen gadget has been used to make breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: To poach is to take what is not yours: the words nutmEG Grater have pocketed an egg. Read straight, it is the familiar morning dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Poaching is cooking gently in simmering water, a common way to prepare an egg for breakfast.

clue.text: Bin moved to fridge

indicators.note: moved means shifted around, so these letters change places

explanation.surface: A bin has been shifted over next to the fridge in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bin' reads as a noun in the surface; it is the verb for throwing away.
explanation.definitionFit: To bin something is to throw it in the rubbish, which is to dispose of it.

clue.text: South African facilities for captive animals, might you say?

indicators.note: asks the solver to voice the words, so the spoken form counts rather than the spelling

parts.note: a loo is a toilet, here one at the zoo

explanation.surface: Asking about the toilets provided for caged creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: A loo is British slang for a toilet; 'facilities' is the polite word for toilets.
explanation.definitionFit: The Zulu are a people of South Africa, so a Zulu is a South African.

clue.text: See 4
Record I request, ultimately wanting sound

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, and ultimately points at the final letter, so the word drops its end

parts.note: a log is a written record
as in a call for help

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a recording but finally finds the sound missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like a noun about audio; it is the adjective meaning reasonable.
explanation.definitionFit: A sound argument is valid and well reasoned, which is what logical means.

clue.text: Reckon tours about to happen — very soon?

indicators.note: to tour is to go around, so one word wraps itself round the other

parts.note: to tot up is to reckon a sum

explanation.surface: Someone thinks a trip is imminent.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: this evening is one thing that is very soon.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonight is later this same day, so it comes very shortly, though not every 'very soon' is tonight.

clue.text: Number one repeated, afraid last on card essential for bingo!

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: inner, as in the inner core of something, its essence

explanation.surface: Bingo-hall talk: the top prize, a nervous wait for the last number on your card.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pulls you into a bingo hall, but 'bingo!' is just the cry of triumph that the casino catchphrase also is.
explanation.definitionFit: The catchphrase is shouted on winning, especially at poker or in video games, just as people shout bingo when they succeed.

clue.text: See 21
Cut off vegetable, typical example

definitions.note: a noun phrase for the norm or standard

indicators.note: something taken off is removed, so a word meaning cut is stripped from the vegetable

parts.note: a parsnip is a root vegetable
a snip is a small cut

explanation.surface: Chopping a vegetable, the normal way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' is not the deletion signal but the letters removed; 'off' does that job.
explanation.definitionFit: Par is the normal or average level, as in 'par for the course', which is the typical case.

clue.text: Bar raised over fifth and sixth of billiard pockets

parts.note: a Mars bar is a chocolate bar

indicators.note: an ordinal picks out the letter at that position counting from the start
an ordinal picks out the letter at that position, here the one straight after the previous pick

explanation.surface: A cue bar lifted over a billiard table's pockets.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' means placed above, so the first pieces come before the letters from billiard. A Mars bar is a chocolate bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Marsupia are the pouches in which marsupials such as kangaroos carry their young, so they are pockets.

clue.text: Greek character, inspiring talker shut up

parts.note: TED talks are the famous inspirational lectures

explanation.surface: A Greek figure breathing in, while some chatterbox is silenced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inspiring' looks like breathing in and so like a container signal; it simply describes the talker.
explanation.definitionFit: Muted means silenced, which is what shut up means as an adjective.

clue.text: Duck à l'orange?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a colourful East Asian duck
second meaning: a small citrus fruit

explanation.surface: The French dish of duck in orange sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: The dish name hides two separate words, each defining the same name; 'à l'' is glue in the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: The mandarin duck is an ornamental bird and the mandarin is a small, loose-skinned orange.

clue.text: Knees-up after a song and dance

explanation.surface: A party that follows a performance of singing and dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: A knees-up is British slang for a lively party. 'Song and dance' looks like a show but is the idiom for a fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: Making a song and dance about something is making a fuss, and ado means fuss.

clue.text: Nappy back in John?

definitions.note: the cloth used to make the nappy
definitions.meaning: first meaning: towelling cloth used for washable nappies
second meaning: the surname of the footballer John, a Chelsea centre-back

explanation.surface: A nappy back in the toilet, a john being American slang for a lavatory.
explanation.walkthrough: John Terry was an England and Chelsea centre-back, so the back of that name is a back. A nappy is a baby's diaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Terry towelling is the looped cloth of old-style nappies; Terry is the surname that follows John.

clue.text: Hack or bug?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an old or worn-out horse

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests computer hacking and bugs; both words have older senses, a horse and to annoy.
explanation.definitionFit: A nag is a poor old horse, as is a hack; to nag someone is to bother them persistently.

clue.text: Sudden drop seen with void when flying

indicators.note: flying letters are scattered through the air and land in a new order

explanation.surface: An aircraft plunges into empty air in a sudden drop.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosedive is a steep downward plunge, of an aircraft or of prices, so a sudden fall.

clue.text: See 13
Villain in opera venue discovered after opening of Rigoletto

indicators.note: dis-covered means with the covering removed, so the outer letters are stripped
the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of the opera's name
La Scala is the opera house in Milan

explanation.surface: A villain in Verdi's Rigoletto turns up at the opera house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' places the stripped venue behind the R.
explanation.definitionFit: A rascal is a rogue or scoundrel, a mild word for a villain.

clue.text: Cold drink containing gas

indicators.note: one item holds the other within it

parts.note: He is the chemical symbol for helium

explanation.surface: A cold drink that is fizzy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cold' looks like an adjective for the drink; it is the noun, the illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheum is the watery discharge from the nose and eyes that a cold produces, so it stands for the cold.

clue.text: One's filling stuffs a turkey in European city

indicators.note: stuffing goes inside, so this letter is pushed into the phrase that follows
a filling is what sits in the middle, so only the central letter is kept

parts.note: central letter of the word one

explanation.surface: Someone stuffing a turkey in a city on the Continent.
explanation.walkthrough: Turkey is slang for a fool or a flop, here an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: Antwerp is a port city in Belgium.

clue.text: Handcuffs piggy individual hasn't got on!

indicators.note: lacking a word spelt the same as on, so those two letters are taken away

explanation.surface: A greedy person in handcuffs but without clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Handcuffs' looks like a plural noun; it is the verb, restricting someone's freedom.
explanation.definitionFit: To handcuff someone figuratively is to restrict them, which is what hampering does.

clue.text: The same doctor cut back

indicators.note: going back means reading the letters right to left
a cut word is shortened, losing its last letter

explanation.surface: The same doctor has suffered a cut to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: Idem is Latin for the same, used in references to repeat a previously cited source.

clue.text: Bevvied Australian, dancing and making whoopee

definitions.note: gerunds standing for the noun: festive revelry

indicators.note: bevvied is British slang for drunk, and a drunk word staggers into a new order

explanation.surface: A drunk Australian dancing and having a wild time.
explanation.walkthrough: Bevvied comes from bevvy, British slang for an alcoholic drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The Saturnalia was the Roman midwinter festival, and the word now means any unrestrained revelry or orgy.
